strategy_title: Autotune XBLOCK to Eliminate Partial Wave Tail
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune with larger XBLOCK configs (256, 512, 1024) to a short-duration pointwise kernel caused a 42% regression (4.42 us → 6.27 us). Although occupancy improved (63% → 77%) and scheduler utilization rose (54% → 82%), the autotuner selected XBLOCK=256 which doubled the register pressure (18 → 31 registers/thread), tripling total executed instructions (917K → 2.85M) and nearly doubling elapsed cycles. The LaunchConfiguration partial-wave penalty (~50% NCU estimate) was not the true bottleneck for this kernel; the kernel was already fast enough that autotune overhead and register spill from larger blocks dominated. For very short kernels (<5 us) with low register counts, adding autotune with larger block sizes can increase register pressure and instruction count enough to negate any wave-tail savings.
slow_pseudocode:
@triton.jit
def kernel(..., XBLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    # XBLOCK=128 fixed, 18 registers/thread
    xoffset = tl.program_id(0) * XBLOCK
    xindex = xoffset + tl.arange(0, XBLOCK)[:]
    # pointwise compute
    tl.store(out_ptr + x3, result, xmask)

grid = (triton.cdiv(xnumel, 128),)  # 2940 blocks, 1.39 waves
kernel[grid](..., XBLOCK=128)
applicable_when: Kernel has many waves with a large partial-wave tail (waves_per_sm >> 2), high register headroom (registers_per_thread << 32), and long duration (>10 us) where wave-tail overhead is a meaningful fraction of runtime.
do_not_apply_when: Kernel duration is short (<5 us); registers_per_thread is already moderate (>15) and larger XBLOCK would push toward register spill; the grid was not updated to use meta['XBLOCK'] (causing the autotuner to always use the fixed grid size regardless of selected config); the kernel is already near the partial-wave boundary with only 1-2 full waves.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune must be paired with a lambda grid (lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(xnumel, meta['XBLOCK']),)) — using a fixed grid defeats the purpose of autotuning block size. In this case the grid was NOT updated to use meta['XBLOCK'], meaning all configs ran with the same 2940-block grid but with different (and larger) XBLOCK values, causing each thread to do more work and increasing register pressure without reducing the grid size.
